subject.title: Feature Request: Add parseMode config for Telegram channels

question: Should Telegram expose a public parse/text-mode selector now, and if so which values and default are supported?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but adding parse-mode config expands a compatibility-sensitive public channel surface and changes how OpenClaw escapes or trusts Telegram-formatted output.

options.title: Approve narrow safe selector
options.body: Add a Telegram plugin config for current HTML versus plain/no-parse delivery, keep the existing default, and defer MarkdownV2/raw HTML/custom emoji semantics to separate decisions.

options.title: Keep current controls only
options.body: Leave formatting on the existing HTML default plus richMessages and markdown.tables controls, and close or defer broader parse-mode selection.

options.title: Fold into broader formatting design
options.body: Handle this together with related Telegram formatting issues such as custom emoji support and configurable reasoning formatting before adding any new public key.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow safe selector
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram plugin config for current HTML versus plain/no-parse delivery, keep the existing default, and defer MarkdownV2/raw HTML/custom emoji semantics to separate decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the HTML formatting behavior and already supplied maintainer-facing review context for this exact issue.
